Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the hosting decision and the network asks for a Private VPC pilot: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary priority: data residency + auditability (SOC2 evidence required)
- Performance: low 90s pct latency at <150ms desired for critical paths
- Economics: evaluating Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC (on-prem/VPC) — leaning toward Private VPC for regulated workloads

Key open items for Private VPC (we need your input)
1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering: which integration model do you prefer for pilot?
2) Egress & allowlist: we need CIDR or a list of egress IPs you can allow; if you want us to provide static egress IPs we can allocate a dedicated pool for your tenant (requires stage allocation).
3) Networking owner & contacts: please share your NetOps point-of-contact (name + email) so we can loop them into the intake.
4) Estimated traffic: rough tokens/day and concurrent requests (p95 QPS) so we size Dedicated or plan capacity for the Private VPC pilot.

Attachments: privatelink_network_diagram.png (network sketch), sla_proposal_v1.pdf (draft SLA + deployment modes comparison)

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm NetOps contact + preferred integration model + a CIDR (or confirm if you'd prefer Redwood-managed egress pool)
- Us (Redwood): open network intake, share sample port list & DNS requirements, and produce a short runbook for allowlist + TLS validation
- Timeline idea: pilot kickoff in mid-Oct, if procurement okays SLA 

If you want, we can also run a short architecture call (30 min) with your NetOps and our infra team next week — propose Tue/Wed mornings (PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the CIDR and contact.

Hi Alex / Aditya — quick technical notes from infra/solutions side to help NetOps scope the work. Short answers first, followed by specifics.

Short recommendations
- Recommended for your pilot: PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoint) if you want minimal routing changes and per-tenant private endpoints. It provides strong isolation and is simpler for NetOps to accept.
- VPC Peering is viable if you want direct L3 connectivity and control of egress; best for long-lived, high-throughput Dedicated deployments.
- Egress: for PrivateLink the outbound requests from our service toward external services (if any) will come from Redwood-managed pools. For traffic inbound to your VPC via PrivateLink, you will not see our egress IPs — you only need to allow the interface endpoint/private DNS. If you require explicit egress IP allowlisting for callbacks (e.g., webhook targets hosted in your VPC) we can allocate a static egress pool for your tenant.

Network specifics (what NetOps will need)
- Ports: 443 (TLS) inbound to the interface endpoint. Outbound (from our infra to your services) typically uses 443. For observability/tracing we may suggest 9411 or 443 depending on the collector (optional).
- DNS: we will provide a private DNS CNAME that points the model endpoint to the interface endpoint; NetOps must accept the private DNS override (no public DNS exposure).
- TLS: TLS mutual-auth is optional; we support standard TLS termination and mutual TLS for customers with stricter auth.
- Egress IPs: if you want static IPs to include in your firewall, tell us whether you prefer: (a) Redwood-managed static pool we reserve for your tenant, or (b) you provide a customer-owned CIDR and we peer/route. For option (a) we assign a /29 or larger depending on expected outbound flows. Exact ranges published after environment allocation.

Next asks from Finsight
- Please complete the network intake form (link below) with: desired integration model (PrivateLink vs Peering), your VPC CIDR (if you want us to peer), and expected peak QPS & tokens/day.
- Provide Samir’s contact and an approval window for mid-Oct for the pilot cutover.

Network intake: https://redwood.ai/network-intake/form/HS-4721

I’ve attached a slightly updated diagram (privatelink_network_diagram.png) that shows the PrivateLink flow and where the egress pool would sit. Marissa — I’ve flagged items that will be part of the runbook (TLS validation steps, sample iptables/route rules).

If helpful, we can spin up a 30-min tech deep-dive with Samir and our infra engineer to walk the diagram and port checks. Propose Tue 21st 9:30am PT.
